issues.description: Inconsistent naming of the Person's first-name field across artifacts: the problem statement and template expect a field/accessor named 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName), whereas the solution's common Person class uses 'givenName' with getGivenName/setGivenName. UI code (PersonScene) and other components rely on the 'firstName' property via reflection (PropertyValueFactory("firstName")). This mismatch is structural and will cause runtime failures (reflection/property binding) and confusion about the correct model API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model consistent across all artifacts. Prefer restoring the template/problem API: rename the field and accessors in the solution's Person class from 'givenName'/'getGivenName'/'setGivenName' to 'firstName'/'getFirstName'/'setFirstName'. Alternatively, update all uses (PersonScene, PropertyValueFactory, and any code referencing firstName) to use 'givenName' consistently. Ensure the model, views, and controllers use the same property names to allow reflection-based binding to work.

issues.description: The Person data model's first name attribute is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement and the template code use the identifier 'firstName' (with getters/setters getFirstName/setFirstName), but the solution repository's common Person class uses 'givenName' (getGivenName/setGivenName). Meanwhile the client views/controllers (PersonScene, etc.) expect 'firstName'. This mismatch makes it unclear which field students should implement and breaks the mapping between the UML/problem description and the solution/template code, causing compilation/runtime confusion when accessing first name properties.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier by renaming the solution repository's Person field and accessors from 'givenName'/'getGivenName'/'setGivenName' to 'firstName'/'getFirstName'/'setFirstName' so that the Person class matches the problem statement, template, and client code. Update any usages accordingly.
